events.text: The Chief Minister of the Six keeps the Seal-Lantern for a single night each year. Tonight it hangs in your hall, and every minister of the Jade Court has a petition they would like read by its light. The queue winds out of the gate and down the White Stairs, all the way to the first cloud.

choices.text: Read them all until dawn, shortest first

effects.log: You read until the wick drops. The short ones are the true ones, you find, and by morning the stairs are empty.

choices.text: Read only the ones from the lowest ranks

effects.log: Eleven clerks weep with relief. Eleven ministers remember who sat behind the Seal-Lantern that night.

choices.text: Take the petitions of the greatest houses first

effects.log: The great houses are grateful in the way weather is grateful. The stair stays full until the lantern dies.

events.text: The Grand Chancellor is old, and tired, and everyone knows it. At the Dragon Table he asks for your opinion on the harvest of the Floating Isles, and the room goes quiet. They are all waiting to see whether the Chief Minister of the Six will say what he wants to hear, or what is true.

choices.text: Say the harvest is thin and ask for relief

effects.log: The Chancellor nods slowly, as if you had confirmed a private fear. Relief is voted before the tea cools.

choices.text: Praise the harvest and keep your own counsel

effects.log: The room exhales. A week later, in a quiet hour, the Chancellor sends a servant with one question: how thin, really.

choices.text: Ask for a year to study the isles first

effects.log: It is not what anyone wanted. It is also what the Chancellor privately needed, and he thanks you in a small way.

events.text: A Minister of the Six, your equal and your rival, has begun hosting a weekly tea for the young scribes of the Archive. They go in nervous and come out loyal. It is a well-run tea. Your own scribes have taken to leaving a little early on tea-days, looking guilty.

choices.text: Host a better tea

effects.log: It costs you an evening a week and a great deal of plum jelly. Within a season the scribes are divided, and cheerful about it.

choices.text: Go to the rival's tea and drink it

effects.log: You arrive without warning and sit among the scribes. The rival pours for you with perfect poise, and the talk is very careful for an hour.

choices.text: Forbid the teas as a distraction from duty

effects.log: The ban holds for a month, and then the teas move to the lotus pool. You have made a story of yourself, not a good one.

events.text: You are a Cloud Sergeant now: eight soldiers, one banner, a stretch of the western cloud-wall to walk every night. The youngest of your eight can barely lift a spear. He is the cousin of a Minister of the Jade Court, and everyone knows it, and he knows they know. He stands very straight.

choices.text: Drill him harder than the rest

effects.log: He cries once, at the end of the first month, and never again. By spring he is the best spear on the wall.

choices.text: Put him on the quietest stretch of wall

effects.log: He thanks you. The other seven watch you do it, and what they think of the Sergeant goes into their faces, and stays there.

choices.text: Write to the Minister and ask him to take the boy home

effects.log: The letter takes a season. The cousin goes home, and the Minister writes back a courteous line.

events.text: The night watch on your stretch of wall brings you a drifting stranger in a torn robe, found clinging to a ledge below the parapet. She says she is a courier. Her papers say she is a courier. Her hands are those of a woman who has not carried a letter in a long time.

choices.text: Hold her until the captain returns

effects.log: She waits calmly, and watches the soldiers go by. When the captain comes, she is gone from her cell, and the door is still locked.

choices.text: Let her go, with a message for the next wall

effects.log: She takes the message, nods once, and steps off the wall into the cloud. A week later a reply arrives, in your own handwriting, from three isles away.

choices.text: Report her and have her sent to the Jade Court

effects.log: You do it properly, with papers. The Court thanks you, and does not tell you what she was.

events.text: Your eight soldiers have a game: whoever loses at knucklebones cleans the sergeant's boots. For three weeks, someone has been losing a lot, and your boots have never been so clean. You suspect the rest of the squad of cheating the tall one, who always loses and never complains.

choices.text: Clean your own boots, and say nothing

effects.log: You wake at dawn and polish them yourself. The squad stops playing. The tall one nods to you, once, on the wall.

choices.text: Take the bones and play the tall one yourself

effects.log: He beats you in four throws. The squad whoops. Your boots shine, and nobody cheats him again.

choices.text: Order the game stopped

effects.log: It stops. So does the singing on the night watch, and the grumbling turns quiet, which is worse.

events.text: A Captain of a Thousand Wings answers for a thousand soldiers and a dozen flying skiffs, and tonight the skiff-wright reports that five of them will not rise. Their lift-stones are cracked. Replacements are on a requisition that will take a season. A raid on the Eastern Isles is expected within the month.

choices.text: Strip three of the skiffs and make two good ones

effects.log: The wright sighs. It takes nine days, and when the raid comes, two skiffs rise and hold the line, and the other three stand empty.

choices.text: Send an urgent requisition to the Marshal, stating the danger plainly

effects.log: You are told to wait. You write again. In the end a crate of stones arrives from the Marshal's own stores, with a note: Do not make me regret this.

choices.text: Fly the five on the cracked stones anyway

effects.log: Two fall out of the sky at the edge of the Eastern Isles. Nobody dies, but the Marshal's note on the incident is very short.

events.text: A Captain of a Thousand Wings from the neighbouring wing, your senior in years and your equal in rank, has taken to sleeping through the dawn muster. His officers cover for him. You are the only one on the wall who has noticed that his banner has not been raised in nine days.

choices.text: Raise his banner yourself, quietly

effects.log: You do it before the dawn bell. He finds out. He says nothing, and never sleeps late again, and never speaks to you of it.

choices.text: Report the matter to the Marshal's office

effects.log: He is replaced within the month. The wing drinks to the new captain. They do not drink to you.

choices.text: Ask him over for a quiet word, and a good wine

effects.log: He tells you about his daughter, who is ill, in the lowlands. You help him arrange leave. His officers begin to look at you differently.

events.text: The thousand are restless. A rumour has swept the barracks that the wing is to be sent to the Storm Reach, where no one comes back, and men and women are quietly writing their wills in the lamplit hours. You know the rumour is false. You also know the Marshal wants it kept quiet.

choices.text: Tell the wing the truth, and take the consequences

effects.log: You assemble them in the yard and tell them. A cheer goes up. The Marshal has you to tea and asks you never to do that again.

choices.text: Keep the Marshal's secret

effects.log: The wills are finished, and the rumour drifts on, and in a month it is a different rumour. Some of your soldiers look at you a little coldly for a year.

choices.text: Issue an order that wills are to be witnessed by the captain

effects.log: It is a way of saying nothing and doing something. The soldiers settle, and you read forty wills, and learn the wing.

events.text: A Cloud Commander leads five thousand from a stone tower on the wall. The tower's upper room has a war-table of white jade, with the isles laid out in chips of coloured stone. A scout has just reported the Eastern Isles in smoke. The chips will not tell you what the smoke means.

choices.text: Send the left wing forward, quickly

effects.log: The smoke is a brush-fire, and the left wing is a day from home. Your officers grin, and you grin, and the Marshal grins at last.

choices.text: Wait, and send three scouts to the smoke

effects.log: The smoke is a signal. Two scouts return. The third brings word that the Marshal was right to be afraid.

choices.text: Call the staff to the war-table and ask them to decide

effects.log: It takes an hour. At the end, the decision is theirs, and so is the credit, and so is the risk.

events.text: One of your five captains, a woman with a scar across her chin, asks for the commander's seal on a leave pass. She has not asked for leave in thirty years. The reason, she says, is a family matter. Her eyes say it is something else. The wing is short-handed.

choices.text: Sign it without asking more

effects.log: She bows lower than the occasion needs. When she returns, she is the best captain you have, for ever after.

choices.text: Ask what the matter is

effects.log: She tells you, in a rush. It is not a family matter. It is a grievance against another officer, and it is a good grievance, and now you have it.

choices.text: Deny it, citing the short roster

effects.log: She takes it with a salute. The roster is filled that month. She does not ask again.

events.text: Your five thousand are good at drilling and bad at feeding themselves. The commissary has been charging the line captains extra for rice, and the extra is not coming back to the wing. You find the ledgers by chance, in a chest, tied with green thread. The commissary master is an old friend.

choices.text: Show him the ledgers, privately

effects.log: He goes grey and says he will put it right. He does, mostly. The friendship takes a chill that lasts a decade.

choices.text: Have the commissary audited by the Marshal's office

effects.log: The audit is thorough and public. The friend is removed. The wing sleeps better. You do not.

choices.text: Burn the ledgers and say nothing

effects.log: The rice goes on costing what it costs. A kind of quiet rot sets into the wing, and you know your own hand is in it.

events.text: A Senior Cloud General is the second voice in the Marshal's tent. Tonight the Marshal is away, and a messenger from the Jade Court has arrived with a sealed order for the full legion to stand down from the Eastern Reach. The seal looks genuine. The order feels wrong.

choices.text: Obey, and stand the legion down

effects.log: The legion stands down. Two days later you learn the order was a forgery. The Marshal never speaks of it, but you are asked to resign your seat on the next council.

choices.text: Hold the order, and send to the Marshal for confirmation

effects.log: It takes six days. The order was real. The Court is furious at your delay. The Marshal, on return, gives you a long look and a small nod.

choices.text: Question the messenger with his own seal-ring in your hand

effects.log: He breaks in an hour. The order is false. You have a name, and a legion at your back, and a moment in which the whole court could change.

events.text: A young staff officer, brilliant and rude, tells you in front of three colonels that your plan for the autumn campaign will fail. He is correct. You have known it for a week. The colonels look at their boots. He does not look away from you.

choices.text: Thank him, and change the plan

effects.log: The colonels are impressed against their will. The staff officer is promoted within the year, and never loses his edge.

choices.text: Dismiss him from the tent

effects.log: He goes. He is right, and the plan fails. Your colonels remember who told you so, and who sent him away.

choices.text: Ask him to stay and propose a better one

effects.log: The plan he draws is better. It is also impossible. Between you, you build a third, and the colonels begin to write notes.

events.text: The widow of a fallen captain comes up the Marshal's Stair on foot, carrying her husband's banner furled in oilcloth. She asks to see the Senior Cloud General. She does not want money. She wants to know, in plain words, how he died. The official report is three lines long.

choices.text: Tell her the whole truth, as far as you know it

effects.log: It is not kind. She listens to every word, nods once, and thanks you. Months later you hear she has asked the same question of every officer on the wall.

choices.text: Give her the official report and an escort home

effects.log: The escort is kind. The widow takes the report, and the banner, and goes. You are never sure what she heard.

choices.text: Order the file reopened

effects.log: The file takes a season. It reveals a small cowardice, someone else's, and a small kindness, the captain's. You send her both.

events.text: A Lord Marshal of a Wing commands a fifth of the Cloud Legion, and on certain nights hears the whole wall breathing in its sleep. Tonight an old sergeant, retired, asks to speak with you alone. He says the Marshal of the whole Legion is making a mistake, and has made it before, and no one has dared tell him.

choices.text: Take the sergeant to the Marshal himself

effects.log: It is a long, awkward audience. The Marshal listens, red to the ears. Afterwards he asks you to dinner, and says nothing about it for years.

choices.text: Hear him out, and keep it to yourself

effects.log: You learn a great deal. You do nothing. A year later the mistake is made again, and you sit in the council with the sergeant's words in your ears.

choices.text: Write it up as a memorandum for the Legion staff

effects.log: The memorandum circulates for a month and is quietly shelved. The sergeant sends a note of thanks anyway.

events.text: Two of your Senior Cloud Generals are feuding, and their feud has begun to spill into the wing. A supply convoy has gone to the wrong isle twice. A patrol has been sent to cover for a patrol that was never asked for. Each comes to you separately, each swearing the other started it.

choices.text: Summon both and make them share a tent for a month

effects.log: They hate it. They come out friends of a sort, and the wing breathes again. Neither forgives you.

choices.text: Reassign one to the far wall

effects.log: The convoys run true. The reassigned general writes you a very polite letter, once a year, for the rest of your life.

choices.text: Find out who really started it

effects.log: It takes weeks. It turns out neither did: a clerk misfiling orders. You promote the clerk, publicly, and the generals stop speaking to each other, and start speaking to you.

events.text: On the eve of the autumn review, the Legion's Marshal has a cough that will not clear. In the privacy of his tent, he asks you, as his most trusted Lord Marshal, whether you would take the baton if it came to that. His eyes are very steady. The tent flap rustles in the wind.

choices.text: Say yes, and mean it

effects.log: He nods. He is quiet a while. At the review he rides the whole length of the line, upright and grim, and the cough does not return that year.

choices.text: Say you would rather he lived to see it

effects.log: He laughs, a dry sound. It is not a refusal and it is not a promise, and he seems to understand both.

choices.text: Say it should go to the best soldier on the wall, whoever that is

effects.log: He looks at you for a long time. He writes a name on a slip of paper and folds it away, and you never learn whose.

events.text: A standard-keeper of the Host carries the banner of a thousand spears, and tonight the banner has been stolen. It hung in the shrine of the barracks on its pole, and now the pole is bare. The captain is furious. The soldiers whisper that the banner has simply gone home, to the god it was woven for.

choices.text: Search the barracks and the shrine floor

effects.log: You find a spool of banner-thread under the altar and a trail of oil leading out the back. The thief is a boy of fourteen, who weaves, and who wanted to see how it was done.

choices.text: Say nothing, and pray at the bare pole

effects.log: Next dawn the banner hangs again, a little damp, smelling of rain. The captain claims a miracle. You keep your counsel.

choices.text: Weave a replacement overnight

effects.log: It is clumsy and crooked. The Host wears it anyway, and the original is never found. The captain commends the stitchwork, grudgingly.

events.text: Your eight spears are posted to the Granary of Pungnyeon, where nothing happens for months at a time. A priest brings a gift of figs each Thursday and a request: that the spears stay out of the granary on Thursdays. You do not ask why. The seventh Thursday, you do.

choices.text: Keep your spears out and your questions to yourself

effects.log: The priest thanks you every week. In winter he sends a jar of honey, and nothing else, and the figs go on.

choices.text: Enter the granary on a Thursday

effects.log: The priest is feeding a hundred poor from the grain, by candlelight, against the Host's rules. You say nothing, and stay to eat.

choices.text: Report the priest to the Captain of the Host

effects.log: He is rebuked, and the poor go hungry for a month. Pungnyeon's next harvest is thin, and you wonder, sometimes, if the god noticed.

events.text: The wall-watch at the edge of the Domain of Mongsa is the quiet kind, with a lot of sleeping soldiers. Tonight yours are all asleep, snoring on their spears, and you are the only one awake. Something walks along the wall: a pale, tall figure, murmuring. It does not seem to see you. It passes through the nearest sleeper.

choices.text: Wake the squad with a shout

effects.log: They tumble up and the figure is gone. Three of them dreamed of the same house that night. You never learn whose house it was.

choices.text: Follow the figure quietly along the wall

effects.log: It stops at the last tower and looks over the edge. You hear a name, softly spoken. Then it is gone, and the wall is only a wall.

choices.text: Stand guard over your sleepers until dawn

effects.log: Nothing returns. In the morning they thank you for letting them rest, not knowing why.

events.text: A captain of a thousand spears commands the Host's Thunder Wing in the Domain of Noegong, where the weather arrives before the orders. Tonight a storm-sergeant reports that every spear in the armoury is humming. The hum rises at dusk. The old priests tell you to move the Host out, now, before the lightning chooses a target.

choices.text: Move the whole wing out to open ground

effects.log: It is a long, wet march. At midnight the armoury is struck, and burns. Nobody is hurt. Everybody agrees you saved the wing.

choices.text: Order every spear laid flat on the earth

effects.log: It is a strange sight: a thousand spears pointing nowhere. The lightning goes elsewhere, and the humming dies. The priests approve.

choices.text: Stay in the armoury with the lamps lit

effects.log: Nothing happens. The humming eases at dawn. You are praised for your courage, and mocked for it in the same breath.

events.text: The god you serve sends a message by dream, as gods do: make peace with the captain of the rival Host across the river. In the morning the dream is gone, but the thought remains. The captain across the river is an old enemy, with a grievance, and a good memory. Both Hosts are watching the ford.

choices.text: Cross the ford alone, unarmed

effects.log: The rival captain meets you halfway with a bowl of rice-wine. It is an awkward hour. By dusk the two Hosts have exchanged banners, and the ford is quiet.

choices.text: Send an offering of peace by a herald

effects.log: The herald returns with a stiff reply. It is not peace, but it is not war either. The ford stays watched.

choices.text: Ignore the dream

effects.log: The dream returns three nights running, each time with the same gentle patience. On the fourth you give in. It is a little late.

events.text: Heaven's Host trains in the courtyard of the Domain, and the sparring is fierce. In the third bout a young spear-bearer of yours takes a hit that breaks his collarbone, and the other captain, a friend of yours, laughs. The spear-bearer is the son of a very minor god. The god is watching from the gallery.

choices.text: Stop the bout and apologise to the minor god

effects.log: The god is mortified, and honoured. The spear-bearer glares at you for a month, and is the best fighter in your thousand by winter.

choices.text: Let the bout continue and say nothing

effects.log: The fight goes on. The minor god leaves quietly, and for a century the Thunder Wing does not forget it.

choices.text: Take the spear-bearer to the healers yourself

effects.log: It is a long walk. By the end of it the boy has stopped glaring. His father, the minor god, sends you a very small, very precise gift.

events.text: A commander of the Host sits at the War Altar of her Domain and receives dreams of battle, which the priests interpret. Tonight the dream is clear, and bad: a field of reeds, a river of silver, and a banner not yours. The priests recommend an immediate march on the Silver Fords. You do not trust the dream.

choices.text: March, as the priests advise

effects.log: The march is hard. At the Silver Fords there is a rival Host, as foretold, and your timing is perfect. The priests are insufferable for a decade.

choices.text: Send scouts first, and sit on the altar

effects.log: The scouts return. The Fords are empty. The dream was a warning for a different year, a different commander. You wonder whose.

choices.text: Ask the priests to dream it again

effects.log: They try three nights in a row. The dream changes each time. By the third night, you are sure it was never about the Fords at all.

events.text: A captain of your thousand has been seen praying at the shrine of a god your Host does not serve. It is not forbidden, quite. But the Host's rule is one banner, one god, and the captain is among the best you have. Her soldiers adore her. She does not hide the shrine visits. She is, if anything, defiant.

choices.text: Confront her privately and listen

effects.log: She is not defiant; she is grieving. The other god keeps a name she lost. You let it be, and she is yours for ever.

choices.text: Forbid it formally

effects.log: She bows, and obeys, and something in her goes out like a lamp. Her thousand are quiet for a season.

choices.text: Declare that every soldier may keep one private shrine

effects.log: There is some grumbling in the high temples. The Host is, by the next year, noticeably more cheerful.

events.text: Your Host has taken a minor fortress at the edge of a quarrelling Domain. In the cellars your quartermaster finds a hoard of offerings: gold, and incense, and little clay animals. The fortress's god has not been seen for centuries. The quartermaster asks, in the careful voice of a man who wants to be told no, what to do with them.

choices.text: Return the offerings to the temple nearby

effects.log: The temple priests weep. The god is not there to be grateful, but a lamp is lit for you that night in the nearest shrine.

choices.text: Divide it among the Host as spoils

effects.log: The soldiers cheer. Twenty years later, in a quiet moment, you wonder if the god will ever come back to ask.

choices.text: Seal the cellar and report it to the Heavenly Court

effects.log: The Court sends a clerk who spends a year counting the clay animals. The Host's name is clean, and a little dull.

events.text: A high general of the Host walks the Marshal's Terrace in the cold before dawn, and tonight finds the god of the Domain walking there too. He is old, and unsure of his name, and he asks you, very politely, whether the Host is still his. The soldiers do not know the god has come. It is a delicate moment.

choices.text: Kneel and swear the Host's service again

effects.log: He is moved, so far as an elder god can be. The next day the Domain's rain comes early, and the Host's granaries are full.

choices.text: Tell him the truth: the Host serves the Court now

effects.log: He nods slowly, as if he had known. He thanks you and walks on. By evening he is gone, and the terrace is cold.

choices.text: Escort him to the nearest temple and ask the priests to decide

effects.log: The priests are overjoyed. The Host is awkwardly at peace with itself for the first time in an age.

events.text: A messenger from the Heavenly Court brings you a list of fourteen gods whose Domains are to be struck from the Host's protection, for want of worship. One of them is the god of a childhood prayer. The list is signed. It is perfectly lawful. It will take effect in three days.

choices.text: Sign the order of withdrawal

effects.log: The thirteen others are no surprise. The fourteenth, you do from duty. That old god sends no sign, and you are never sure whether that is forgiveness.

choices.text: Petition the Court to spare that one Domain

effects.log: The petition is refused. It is also noted. In the next review, the Domain's worshippers number one more, and the Host stays.

choices.text: Send the Host to the Domain quietly, as an exercise

effects.log: There is no order against exercises. The Host camps there for a year, and the worshippers, seeing banners, return.

events.text: A young spear of the Host salutes you at the training ground, and says he is the son of the woman you once left behind to hold a pass. You remember the pass. You remember her last message, and you remember that you did not read it until the next day. He is polite and he is waiting.

choices.text: Tell him everything

effects.log: It takes the whole afternoon. At the end he says, simply, that he understands, and is quiet a long while. Then he asks to serve under you.

choices.text: Tell him she died well

effects.log: It is true, as far as it goes. He thanks you and salutes. You watch him go with an old stone in your chest.

choices.text: Give him her last message, which you have kept

effects.log: He reads it by the lamp-post, in the dusk, with his lips moving. When he looks up, he is no longer a boy.

events.text: A lord marshal of a wing of Heaven keeps the Gate of the Seventh Domain, where the Host's oldest banners hang in the Hall of Standards. Tonight a priest of the Court shows you a blank banner, new-woven, and says it is for the next war. He does not say which war. His eyes are very bright.

choices.text: Refuse to receive it

effects.log: He bows, and the banner is taken away. For a century afterwards the Hall of Standards feels a little lighter.

choices.text: Hang it in the Hall, unmarked

effects.log: It hangs there for a long age, blank, and visitors stop to look at it. No one is ever sure why.

choices.text: Ask the priest which war it is for

effects.log: He will not say. But he blinks, once, in a way that you read afterward as a warning, and you begin quietly to increase the Host's training.

events.text: Two gods of neighbouring Domains have each sent you a gift: a spear, a jewelled banner. Each asks, with perfect courtesy, that the Host favour them in the coming council. You are a lord marshal. You have neither a Domain nor a cause. The two gifts sit side by side on your table, glittering.

choices.text: Return both with courteous notes

effects.log: Neither god forgets. Both treat you thereafter with the careful respect due to a power that is not for sale.

choices.text: Keep both, and favour neither

effects.log: You display them together in the Hall. It is a small, wry joke that both gods seem to understand, and both enjoy.

choices.text: Keep the spear and give the banner to the Host

effects.log: It is a favour to one, and a gesture to all. The council goes well, and a certain coolness settles over one of the gods.

events.text: On the festival of the Host, the soldiers of every wing march past the lord marshals' dais, and tonight you notice that a hundred of them are very young, scarcely more than children, in armour that does not fit. They are new to the Host, drawn from the dying Domains. You are lord marshal; their training is, in the end, yours to set.

choices.text: Add a year of schooling to their first term

effects.log: The Court grumbles at the cost. The young ones fight better, and write better, and stay.

choices.text: Pair each with a veteran for the first season

effects.log: It works, mostly. The veterans complain, then adopt their charges with ferocity. A bond forms that lasts for ages.

choices.text: Send them to the quiet walls until they grow into their armour

effects.log: They grow. Several do not grow quickly enough, and the Host quietly loses them. You stand at their memorial each year.

events.text: The high steward of the kingdom keeps the keys to every storehouse from the northern salt-works to the southern orchards. At the turn of the year the keys are counted aloud before the king and the council, each in turn, and tonight the count comes to one short. Everyone in the hall looks at you, politely, not breathing.

choices.text: Own the loss, and offer to search every storehouse

effects.log: It takes a month. The key is found in a miller's apron, forgotten by a clerk. The king laughs. The council remembers that you offered to look.

choices.text: Declare the count correct and say the keys are in the king's trust

effects.log: There is a long silence. The king nods. Whatever happened to the key is settled quietly, and your voice is treated carefully thereafter.

choices.text: Ask the council to recount, slowly, with you

effects.log: The recount finds a miscounted key, in the second row. The steward of the keys was the one who miscounted. He is gently moved to another post.

events.text: A delegation from the neighbouring kingdom arrives at the high steward's door with a gift of a thousand sheep, and a request: a quiet word, about the border pastures, that never reaches the council. They are courteous, and well-fed, and they will be here until you answer.

choices.text: Take the sheep and keep the word

effects.log: A scandal in miniature, which blows over in a season. You never eat mutton again.

choices.text: Send the sheep back and bring the matter to the council

effects.log: The neighbours are offended, and then, a month later, wary and respectful. The council sees the matter in the open.

choices.text: Give the sheep to the border villages and keep the word

effects.log: The villages are puzzled and delighted. The neighbours, informed, are quietly furious. You have bought yourself a long watchfulness.

events.text: The chancellor of the kingdom is dying, slowly and in public, and everyone knows who will succeed: you, or the treasurer. The treasurer has begun giving banquets. Your own table is quiet. The chancellor sends a message: come and read to him on the evenings you can, because his eyes are going.

choices.text: Go every evening, and read whatever he asks

effects.log: It is mostly poetry and old tax-law. You learn a great deal about the kingdom, and he about you. When he dies, he leaves you his notes.

choices.text: Host a banquet to match the treasurer's

effects.log: It is a great success, and costs more than you intended. The chancellor, hearing of it, sends a short letter which you keep.

choices.text: Do your work, visit now and then, and let the succession decide itself

effects.log: The succession decides itself. It is a quiet, clean decision, and you are honest with yourself about why.

events.text: You are a sergeant of the levy now, with seven soldiers in a village that is mostly fields. The village headman has asked you, kindly, to bring your squad to the harvest, as the sickles are few. Your orders say nothing about harvesting. The grain is ripe. The rain is three days off.

choices.text: Take the squad into the fields

effects.log: Seven soldiers and a wagon of grain. The headman weeps. The captain, hearing of it, writes a very short letter that says nothing at all.

choices.text: Keep to the orders and drill as usual

effects.log: The harvest is saved by the village alone, barely. The squad drills in silence, watching the gold fields.

choices.text: Ask the captain by messenger for leave

effects.log: The reply comes in two days: Do what is sensible. You do. You take full credit for the captain's wisdom, in the village.

events.text: One of your seven, a thin boy from the hill villages, cannot march in step. He is always a half-beat late, never early, as though he were hearing a different drum. The others laugh. He does not. In a skirmish with bandits last week, he was the only one who heard them coming.

choices.text: Excuse him from marching, and make him your scout

effects.log: He is a superb scout. The squad stops laughing within the season. He marches in a ragged sort of time, ever after, and is not corrected.

choices.text: Drill him until he keeps step

effects.log: It takes a month. He keeps step. He also stops hearing the bandits, or says he does, and you are never sure what you cost him.

choices.text: Let him be, and have the others learn his step

effects.log: It is a good joke for a month. By winter the squad marches half a beat late, together, and is mysteriously hard to ambush.

events.text: The ferry at the river-crossing is run by an old woman who will carry your levy across for nothing, if you will listen to her story first. It is always the same story, about a drowned son and a bargain with a river-spirit. Your squad has heard it eleven times. She starts again.

choices.text: Listen to it properly this time

effects.log: It is the same story, but today there is a detail you missed: the bargain was not broken. You ask her about it, gently. She speaks for an hour, and the ferry is free for ever.

choices.text: Have the squad cross by the upstream ford instead

effects.log: It is cold and wet and takes an hour. The old woman watches from the bank. You feel her disappointment like a draught.

choices.text: Pay her a small coin and skip the story

effects.log: She takes the coin with dignity. She tells the story to the empty bank as you leave.

events.text: A good captain of a thousand in the levy knows every one of a hundred sergeants by their boots, and you are trying to be one. Tonight the quartermaster reports that boots for the whole thousand will be late by two months, and it is nearly winter. Your sergeants are already muttering, in the barracks, about the council that will not pay for good leather.

choices.text: Go yourself to the bootmakers' guild and strike a bargain

effects.log: You spend three days in the guild hall. The boots arrive in a month, rough but sound. The guild-master asks you to dinner.

choices.text: Order the thousand to make their old boots last, and share a spare pair per squad

effects.log: It is a hard winter. The thousand sing a rude song about you, and march through snow in shared leather.

choices.text: Write to the high steward and explain the matter plainly

effects.log: The high steward replies with the exact number of pairs, and a signature. The boots are in the yard within the fortnight.

events.text: A rival captain, commanding the thousand next to yours, claims credit in the council for a mountain pass your squads cleared last spring. He has a good voice, and a good memory for other people's work. The council is listening. You are in the gallery, and you have a choice of how to stand.

choices.text: Stand up and correct him in front of the council

effects.log: The room is silent. He retreats, graceless, and you gain a reputation for fairness and a lasting enemy.

choices.text: Wait until the session ends and ask to speak with him privately

effects.log: He is polite, even apologetic. The next day, the council hears a gentler version of the story, with your name in it.

choices.text: Let it stand, and take the credit that matters from your own soldiers

effects.log: They notice. They say nothing, but they march as though the pass were theirs, which it is.

events.text: The mother of one of your soldiers has come to the camp to ask whether her son is alive. He is. He is also in the guardhouse for striking a sergeant. The woman is old, travel-stained, and has walked from the far valleys. She asks to see him. Rules say the guardhouse is closed to visitors until sentence.

choices.text: Let her in, with yourself as escort

effects.log: They sit together an hour. Neither speaks much. When she leaves, she touches your sleeve, and your soldier never strikes a sergeant again.

choices.text: Explain the rule and give her a meal in the mess

effects.log: She eats, and sleeps, and goes in the morning with a message from her son, which you carry. It is a kindness, of a kind.

choices.text: Hasten the sentence so she can see him

effects.log: The sentence is lighter than it might have been, and sooner. The sergeant he struck is not pleased, but is in no position to say so.

events.text: A commander of the levy answers to the kingdom for five thousand mouths and their spears. Tonight the high steward's courier arrives with new orders: march at once to the western marches, where a border village has called for help. The roads are bad, the weather worse, and the village is not on any map the army owns.

choices.text: March at dawn with the whole levy

effects.log: The march is miserable. The village is real, and its need is real, and the grateful headman names a field after you.

choices.text: Send a fast column of five hundred first

effects.log: The column arrives in time. The levy follows more slowly. The village is saved, and the council notes your prudence.

choices.text: Question the courier, and the orders, closely

effects.log: The courier is young and nervous. The orders are genuine, but the village's name is spelled two ways. You send a rider ahead to confirm, and are right to.

events.text: Your five captains meet in the commander's tent each month. Tonight one of them, the quietest, proposes a plan so bold that the others fall silent. It is clever. It is also dangerous, and would, if it failed, end the levy. The captain has clearly thought of nothing else for a year.

choices.text: Approve it, and take responsibility

effects.log: The plan works, narrowly. The quiet captain becomes the loudest in the tent, and a lifelong friend.

choices.text: Ask the captain to prepare a more cautious version

effects.log: It is a good version. The quiet captain, hurt at first, comes round. The levy lives to fight another year.

choices.text: Reject it and say nothing more

effects.log: The captain bows and goes. The levy does not fail. It does not grow either. For some years there is a quiet in the tent that was not there before.

events.text: Peace has lasted four years, and the levy has grown fat. The council proposes reducing its numbers by half, and the commander of the levy is asked to attend and defend its size. The treasurer speaks first, with figures. The room listens. When it is your turn, you realise you have nothing prepared but the truth.

choices.text: Speak plainly of what the levy has done and might do

effects.log: The council listens. The cut is reduced to a third. The treasurer does not forgive you, but respects your plain speech.

choices.text: Offer to cut the levy by half and keep the best of it

effects.log: It is a hard bargain. The best are kept; the rest are sent home with a small pension and a bad taste in many mouths.

choices.text: Ask for a year to show that the levy can feed itself

effects.log: You are given the year. The levy farms, and builds, and mends roads, and is not cut.

events.text: A high general of the kingdom is the voice the king asks for in the dark. Tonight the king sends for you, alone, and shows you a letter from a neighbouring kingdom proposing a marriage alliance. It would mean peace for a generation. It would also mean, as the king puts it, handing a daughter to a stranger. He asks what you think.

choices.text: Advise the alliance, and accept the risk of the peace

effects.log: The marriage is made. It is a hard match, and a lasting one. The border is quiet for forty years.

choices.text: Advise against it, and ready the levy

effects.log: The refusal is courteous. A season later the neighbours muster at the border, and you are glad you were right, and sorry.

choices.text: Ask the king to put it to the princess

effects.log: The king is startled. The princess, who is wiser than anyone expected, says yes, with conditions. The conditions are good ones.

events.text: An old comrade, a captain from your first campaign, asks for the high general's help in a private matter: a debt, a pardon, a quiet word. It is a small thing, as these things go, and a wrong thing. He does not ask lightly. He sits very still, hat in hand, in your study.

choices.text: Grant it, and trust the old friendship

effects.log: It is a small favour. It is also the first of many, and one day the council notices.

choices.text: Refuse, and explain why, as a friend

effects.log: He takes it badly, then well. A year later he sends a bottle of the old wine, and a message: You were right. He never asks for anything again.

choices.text: Find a lawful way to help him

effects.log: It takes weeks, and most of the favours you have. The debt is paid, the pardon is real, and you are a little poorer in goodwill.

events.text: Your high general's tent is the best-lit place in the camp, and every officer comes to it to be seen. Tonight a young lieutenant, a stranger, comes in and asks for nothing: only to watch you work. He sits in the corner for an hour and takes notes, and leaves. You learn later that he is the king's spy.

choices.text: Let it be known you welcome observers

effects.log: The word spreads. The king, hearing of it, is amused, and the lieutenant returns, this time with a smile.

choices.text: Have the lieutenant followed

effects.log: He is skilled and untraceable. You gain a certain unease, and the king gains a certain opinion of your suspicion.

choices.text: Prepare a clear account of the campaign for the king, in writing

effects.log: The account is read aloud in council. It is thorough, honest, and a little dry. The king nods, and the spy is withdrawn.

events.text: A lord marshal of the kingdom sits at the right hand of the king at war councils, and on the last night of the autumn the king asks you to walk with him along the wall. He speaks little. At the third tower he stops and says that he is thinking of making you regent of the realm while he travels abroad. He does not ask. He merely mentions.

choices.text: Accept, and swear to protect the throne

effects.log: The king nods. It is a sober honour, and a heavy one. The council watches with long faces.

choices.text: Ask who else he has considered

effects.log: He tells you. It is a short list, and you recognise two of the names with a sinking feeling. You tell him what you think of each.

choices.text: Decline, and recommend the queen

effects.log: He is silent a long time, and then he laughs, and says that he had hoped you would. The queen is told that night.

events.text: The kingdom's oldest banner, the one the first levy marched under, hangs in the hall of the marshals. Tonight, by lamplight, you notice a rent in it, small and old, running through the red. It has been there longer than you have. A page tells you shyly that the banner has been mended nine times, always in secret, always on the same night.

choices.text: Learn who has been mending it

effects.log: It is an old woman, a seamstress, who lives in a hut by the wall. She has done it for forty years. You thank her; she is puzzled by the fuss.

choices.text: Order the banner mended openly, in the hall, by all the marshals

effects.log: It is a clumsy ceremony. It is also, you realise afterward, the first time the marshals have done anything together in years.

choices.text: Leave the rent as it is

effects.log: It is a quiet decision. In time visitors stop at the tear, and ask, and are told the story. You are told it is your doing.

events.text: The marshal of the kingdom is dead. In the hall of the marshals, three lord marshals stand around the bier: you, and two others. The king has not yet named a successor. One of the others looks at you with a frankly measuring eye. The other looks at the floor. Whoever is named, the three of you will need to live with it.

choices.text: Speak first, and say that you will serve whoever is named

effects.log: It is a clean, plain thing to say. The one who was measuring you blinks. The other looks up, and nods.

choices.text: Say nothing, and wait for the king's word

effects.log: The silence lasts an hour. When the king arrives, the three of you bow together, and no one has promised anything.

choices.text: Withdraw from consideration, in the king's presence, before he can decide

effects.log: It is bold, and a little theatrical. The king respects it. You are not named, and you are not forgotten.
